surname_desc: Choi (崔) is Korea's fourth most common surname at about 4.7%. The principal Gyeongju Choi clan traces to Choi Chi-won, a celebrated Silla-era scholar revered as the father of Korean literature.

short: Someone with an abundant, sky-wide heart
meaning: 다민 (多旻, Damin) joins 다 (多, da), "abundant," with 민 (旻, min), "the wide sky." It pictures someone with an abundant, sky-wide heart. Clear and fresh, its sleek 민 (as in 지민, Jimin) suits anyone. Abundance and modern polish give it a bright, trendy feel.
surname_desc: Ko (高) is Korea's 22nd most common surname at about 0.9%. The Jeju Ko clan is legendary — one of the three founding families said to have emerged from the earth on Jeju Island.

short: Someone wise and high in virtue
meaning: 예성 (叡聖, Yeseong) joins 예 (叡, ye), "bright and wise," with 성 (聖, seong), "sacred and virtuous." It's a boy's name meaning someone wise and high in virtue. K-pop fans know it as Yesung of Super Junior — nicknamed for an "artistic voice" — a refined, gifted impression.
surname_desc: Kim (金) is Korea's most common surname, held by about 21.5% of the population — roughly one in five Koreans. The major lineages, the Gimhae and Gyeongju Kim clans, trace back to Silla royalty.

short: Someone holy as a model
meaning: 해성 (楷聖, Haeseong) pairs 해 (楷, hae), "model, exemplary," with 성 (聖, seong), "virtuous and saintly." It also evokes 혜성, "comet," the image of a brilliant streak across the night sky. Firm and upright, exemplariness, virtue, and comet-like brilliance meet in a confident name.
surname_desc: Moon (文) is Korea's 23rd most common surname at about 0.9%. The character means 'literature, writing' — fittingly, the Nampyeong Moon clan produced many distinguished scholars.
